Beyond the obvious · twice-weekly edit

Unusual London events,
this week.

Discover free and affordable things to do in London this week and weekend, selected for unusual access, local character and a story worth following. Every listing is checked against the official organiser before publication.

Friday 23 October – Sunday 25 October · Last edited 22 October at 15:02

The complete edit

8 verified events
Friday 23 October1 event
Local culture Free

12:00–20:00

God Save the Queens: Women Who Made Punk

A landmark basement-gallery show opens with personal archives, photography, fashion and unheard stories from Poly Styrene and the women who shaped punk's visual language.

Venue
Museum of Youth Culture
Address
51 St Pancras Way, London, NW1 0PU
Access
Booking recommended
Check official details ↗
Saturday 24 October3 events
Heritage & history Free

10:30–16:00

Home Movie Day at the Cinema Museum

Film archivists examine 8mm, Super 8, 9.5mm and 16mm home movies, offer preservation advice and project selected reels alongside a 1970s family-film programme.

Venue
The Cinema Museum
Address
2 Dugard Way, off Renfrew Road, London, SE11 4TH
Access
Drop in
Check official details ↗
Heritage & history Free

12:00–18:00

Reclaiming the Archives at Fulham Palace

A palace walk, historical workshops, poetry and zine-making confront a Royal African Company pamphlet with a 1723 letter written by an enslaved person known as Secrett.

Venue
Fulham Palace
Address
Bishop's Avenue, Fulham, London, SW6 6EA
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Local culture Free

18:00–21:30

Mon Âme: Black Life on Film

A free community screening pairs Mon Âme with films on Black life and representation, followed by a discussion about cultural memory and the future of East End communities.

Venue
Oxford House Theatre
Address
Derbyshire Street, Bethnal Green, London, E2 6HG
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Sunday 25 October4 events
Heritage & history Free entry

10:00–18:00

Big Story Festival at IWM London

IWM London's first storytelling festival fills the museum with free illustration, play and song sessions shaped by its Childhood in War exhibition; selected talks cost extra.

Venue
IWM London
Address
Lambeth Road, London, SE1 6HZ
Access
Drop in

Art & design £10 per person

11:30–14:30

The Enchanted Cinema: The Music of Spirit Animals

Children and grown-ups become a live sound-effects orchestra for animations inspired by Día de Muertos, global folklore and the Horniman's animal collections. Two one-hour Sunday sessions.

Venue
Horniman Museum and Gardens, Pavilion
Address
100 London Road, Forest Hill, London, SE23 3PQ
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Heritage & history Free; pumpkin £3

13:00–16:00

Halloween at Brixton Windmill

A 200-year-old working windmill hosts free crafts and children's spooky stories inside the mill, with optional traditional pumpkin carving for £3.

Venue
Brixton Windmill and Windmill Gardens
Address
Blenheim Gardens, Brixton, London, SW2 5DA
Access
Drop in

Local culture Free

13:00–19:00

Diwali on the Square 2026

Trafalgar Square becomes a shared Festival of Light with 200 opening dancers, performances from London's Hindu, Sikh and Jain communities, workshops and food stalls.

Trafalgar Square

Trafalgar Square, Westminster, London, WC2N 5DN
